subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Lino printing is an example of which type of printmaking?
questions.explain: In relief printing such as lino, ink sits on the raised surface while cut-away areas stay blank.

questions.q: What is the secondary colour made by mixing red and yellow?
questions.explain: Red mixed with yellow produces the secondary colour orange.

questions.q: What does adding white to a colour create?
questions.explain: Adding white to a colour produces a tint (a lighter version), while adding black produces a shade.

questions.q: Screen printing pushes ink through what?
questions.explain: Screen printing forces ink through a fine mesh, with a stencil blocking areas that stay unprinted.

questions.q: Which 3D technique is additive, building up a form from a soft material?
questions.explain: Modelling adds and shapes pliable material such as clay to build up a form.
The 'B' scale denotes softer, darker pencils, so 6B is much softer and darker than an H grade.

questions.q: Collage is an artwork made by...
options: Sticking different materials onto a surface
questions.explain: Collage assembles and glues various materials, such as paper or fabric, onto a surface.

questions.q: A 'hue' refers to which property of colour?
options: The pure colour itself, such as red or blue
questions.explain: Hue is the name of the pure colour, such as red, yellow or blue, before tints or shades are added.

questions.q: What is the key difference between shape and form?
options: Shape is large, form is small
Shape is coloured, form is not
Shape is two-dimensional, form is three-dimensional
questions.explain: A shape is flat and two-dimensional, while a form has depth and appears three-dimensional.

questions.q: Which paint is water-based and dries quickly to a permanent finish?
questions.explain: Acrylic paint is water-based, dries fast and becomes water-resistant once dry.

questions.q: The rule of thirds suggests you place key features where?
options: In the exact centre of the image
Around the edges of the frame
Along lines that divide the image into thirds or at their intersections
questions.explain: The rule of thirds divides the picture into a 3x3 grid and places focal points on the lines or intersections.

questions.q: In a mono-print, how many prints can usually be taken from one inking?
questions.explain: A mono-print produces a single, unique image, unlike editions made from a fixed block or plate.
